figures.label: Bilateral trade, FY 2024-25
figures.note: India's exports USD 2.1 billion, imports USD 1.6 billion. The brief records that trade fell in this year.

figures.label: Agricultural Centres of Excellence
figures.note: Operating under the sixth work plan, covering 2024 to 2026.

figures.label: Israeli foreign direct investment into India
Jews of Indian origin in Israel
figures.note: The Ministry of External Affairs brief of February 2026 records over 100,000. The Embassy of India in Tel Aviv records approximately 85,000. This site shows both rather than picking one.

figures.label: Indian citizens in Israel
figures.note: The Ministry of External Affairs brief records over 42,000. The Embassy page records about 18,000, described as mainly caregivers, diamond traders, information technology professionals and students. The two figures may be counting different populations or different periods.

figures.label: Jews living in India
figures.note: Figure for 2020. Earlier estimates recorded between 4,900 and 7,000 as of 1996.

figures.label: Bilateral trade, the whole series
figures.note: About USD 200 million in 1992, almost all diamonds. USD 7.86 billion in FY 2021-22. A peak of USD 10.77 billion in FY 2022-23. USD 6.53 billion in FY 2023-24. USD 3.75 billion in FY 2024-25. The rise and the fall are both steep, and the fall is attributed in the Ministry brief to regional security issues and trade disruption.

figures.label: Trade in FY 2024-25, two official figures
figures.note: The Ministry of External Affairs records USD 3.75 billion. The Press Information Bureau records approximately USD 3.62 billion. Both are Indian government sources for the same financial year.

figures.label: Israel's share of Indian arms imports, 2020 to 2024
figures.note: Third largest supplier after Russia at 36 per cent and France at 33 per cent. India was the second largest arms importer in the world over that period.

figures.label: The India-Israel innovation fund
figures.note: Twenty million dollars from each side. Established after the July 2017 visit, ran from 2018 to 2022, renewed for 2023 to 2027. Thirty-four projects funded.

figures.label: Farmers trained at the Centres of Excellence
figures.note: Stated in the joint statement of 26 February 2026. An earlier count, in June 2022, recorded more than 3.6 lakh farmers trained and over 250 field officers trained in Israel.

figures.label: Indian workers in Israel under the framework agreement
figures.note: As of 1 July 2025, comprising 6,730 in construction and 44 caregivers. Counting private recruitment channels as well, the Indian government's parliamentary reply puts the total transferred between November 2023 and July 2025 at more than 20,000.

figures.label: Additional Indian workers agreed in February 2026
figures.note: Agreed for arrival within five years, with implementation protocols signed for commerce and services, restaurants, and manufacturing.

figures.label: Total bilateral investment, September 2025
figures.note: The figure stated when the Bilateral Investment Agreement was signed.

questions.q: Why did India recognise Israel in 1950 but wait until 1992 for full diplomatic relations?
questions.note: Forty-two years is the longest unexplained interval in the relationship. Any account of India and Israel that skips it is not an account.

questions.q: What did the copper plates of Kerala actually grant, and to whom?
questions.note: The plates are the closest thing to a dated primary document in the early history of Jews in India.

questions.q: Are Bene Israel origin traditions historically testable at all?
questions.note: Community memory and documentary history are different kinds of evidence. The interesting question is what happens where they meet.

questions.q: Is the relationship becoming more technological than military?
questions.note: Agriculture, water and innovation funding have grown alongside defence. Which one defines the next decade is genuinely open.

questions.q: Why did bilateral trade fall in FY 2024-25?
questions.note: The Ministry of External Affairs brief records the fall. The reasons are worth documenting rather than assuming.

questions.q: Why do official Indian sources give different diaspora figures?
questions.note: Over 100,000 and approximately 85,000 appear in two Indian government sources. The gap itself is a research question.

questions.q: What did migration to Israel change for the communities that left?
questions.note: Four communities, four different trajectories, one destination.

questions.q: How has India imagined Israel, and how has Israel imagined India?
questions.note: Both countries carry an image of the other that predates any embassy.

scenarios.title: The trade turn
scenarios.body: The free trade agreement, whose terms of reference were agreed in November 2025, becomes the organising fact of the relationship, and commerce outgrows defence.

scenarios.title: Water and climate
scenarios.body: Scarcity does what diplomacy could not. Desalination, reuse and desert agriculture become the shared frontier as both countries face harder water years.

scenarios.title: The corridor
scenarios.body: Haifa, the Arabian Sea and the Mediterranean are stitched into one logistics chain, and the relationship becomes a question of infrastructure.

scenarios.title: Deep technology
scenarios.body: Innovation funding, joint research and startup capital carry the relationship, and the centre of gravity moves from governments to firms and laboratories.

scenarios.title: Civilisational exchange
scenarios.body: Chairs, archives, translation and scholarship build a durable intellectual link that survives changes of government on both sides.

scenarios.title: The plateau
scenarios.body: The relationship consolidates at its present level. Agreements are renewed, dialogues continue, and nothing fundamental changes.
